title: Right-context loss breaks matched-left ties but transfers unevenly to fresh contrasts
statement: I froze a bilateral-context discriminator and its calibration cutoffs before evaluating fresh reference-text controls. The score averages Jensen-Shannon divergences between candidate/first-component left contexts and candidate/second-component right contexts. With exact left-context matching, genuine candidates beat decoys in 24/30 evaluation repeats across six contrasts; the left-only and inherited eight-rule losses tie in every repeat. The frozen bilateral cutoff accepts 14 genuine candidates and zero decoys. However, us/um fails in all five repeats, word-position-only matching gives just 16/30 genuine wins, and exact matching of both sides forces ties. This supports a conditional improvement, not a general glyph-composition test. No manuscript triplets were evaluated.
check: Recover plan.json byte-for-byte from reproduction.plan_json_bytes and both frozen scripts in one scratch directory. From the repository root on PYTHONPATH, run right_context.py calibrate, then right_context.py evaluate. Check the plan, script, calibration and evaluation digests and tables; run verify_right_context.py for the independent entropy/sampling audit. A next test should calibrate contextual and word-position conditioning on new contrasts before any manuscript use, particularly investigating the repeatable us/um reversal. All weights, cutoffs, contrasts and seed lists in this experiment remain frozen.

plan.hypothesis: Adding candidate right-context similarity to the proposed second component improves genuine-versus-decoy discrimination under matched immediate left contexts.

scores.eight_rule_prose: Previous P-L1-007 eight-rule prose implementation, unchanged; raw loss, not its original rank percentile.

plan.js_definition: Equal-weight Jensen-Shannon divergence, log base 2, sum only nonzero probability terms, no smoothing, raw adjacency counts including spaces. Requires nonempty distributions; singleton distributions are valid.
plan.partitioning: Calibration: first 40000 characters from refcorpus.calib_text, drop final partial word. Evaluation: refcorpus.control_text beginning at character 40000, drop first partial word, take at most 40000 further characters and drop final partial word. Surround each text with a space. These control blocks follow the prefix used in the earlier audit.
plan.pairing: Find target AB and decoy AD in words. Match word-initial and word-final position flags. Additional modes match previous glyph (left) or previous and next glyph (both). Shuffle groups and pair lists with each fixed seed. Accept edits only when starts differ by at least 3 and are not within 2 positions of a previous accepted start. Replace the target by X and decoy by Z in one shared text.
plan.eligibility: At least 40 occurrences of each engineered candidate and each proposed component A,B in the encoded text; nonempty incoming/outgoing distributions. No minimum distinct-context count. Report excluded conditions.
plan.paired_comparison: A genuine win means score(X,A,B) < score(Z,A,B) - 1e-12. Reverse inequality is a decoy win; otherwise tie. Report by language and contrast; seeds are robustness replicates, not independent samples.
plan.threshold: For each score, pool eligible calibration primary-condition decoy losses. Sort n losses; set cutoff to loss at zero-based index floor(0.05*n). Accept only loss < cutoff - 1e-12. This attains at most 5% empirical calibration decoy acceptance, allowing ties. Freeze cutoff file and its digest in the public branch before evaluating controls. If no eligible calibration negatives exist, report unavailable and do not improvise.
plan.negative_controls: On untouched evaluation streams and 20 new direct-emission first-order character chains per language, score every letter C not A or B with at least 40 occurrences, using the same fixed components and cutoff. Fit chains on the first 40000 complete-word characters of refcorpus.train_text. Emit exactly 40000 glyphs from one table with sampled starts; end on a nonspace glyph. Each case has no pair-fusion operation. Report candidate-level counts and sample-level any-acceptance separately; samples/contrasts share data.
plan.manuscript_gate: Do not evaluate manuscript candidate triplets in this experiment. A positive result on these selected controls would still need new language/text and scan validation.
plan.stop_rule: No weight, contrast, seed, cutoff rule, sample window, support or matching change after observing outcome. Bugs require a documented amendment and a new plan hash.

scripts.reproduce.py:
"""Extract the submitted protocol and reproduce byte-identical Windows outputs.

Run from the repository root: python reproduce.py STEP_JSON SCRATCH_DIRECTORY
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

submission = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
scratch = Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve()
scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
(scratch/'plan.json').write_bytes(submission['reproduction']['plan_json_bytes'].encode('utf-8'))
for name, script in submission['reproduction']['scripts'].items():
    (scratch/name).write_bytes(script.encode('utf-8'))
env = dict(os.environ)
env['PYTHONPATH'] = str(Path.cwd()) + os.pathsep + env.get('PYTHONPATH', '')
def digest(name):
    actual = hashlib.sha256((scratch/name).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert actual == submission['output_digests'][name], (name, actual)
for name in ('plan.json', 'right_context.py', 'original_triplet.py'):
    digest(name)
for command, output in [(['right_context.py', 'calibrate'], 'calibration.json'),
                         (['right_context.py', 'evaluate'], 'evaluation.json'),
                         (['verify_right_context.py'], 'verification.json')]:
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-X', 'utf8', str(scratch/command[0]), *command[1:]],
                   env=env, check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    # Original outputs used native Windows CRLF. Preserve their published raw hashes
    # across operating systems; the frozen measurement code is left untouched.
    path = scratch/output
    path.write_bytes(path.read_bytes().replace(b'\r\n', b'\n').replace(b'\n', b'\r\n'))
    digest(output)
    print(output, 'exact digest matched', flush=True)

reproduction.instructions: Extract reproduce.py from the scripts dictionary, then from the repository root run python reproduce.py /path/to/step.json /path/to/scratch. It saves the exact embedded input bytes, runs calibration then evaluation and independent verification, and checks all six raw file hashes. Original plan/original_triplet.py and JSON outputs use Windows CRLF; the runner preserves/normalizes those line endings for byte-identical cross-platform reproduction without changing frozen measurement code or thresholds. Full negative-candidate output is recreated as evaluation.json; the submission retains all paired rows and per-negative-stream/contrast minima and accepted candidates.

findings: On the primary calibration condition (exact-left matching, full matched-pool replacement), all 30 paired trials favor the genuine candidate under bilateral JS. The automatically chosen cutoff is 0.13251493881410006, with strict loss < cutoff-1e-12 acceptance. It accepts 15/30 genuine candidates and 1/30 calibration decoys. This empirical calibration count does not establish a population error rate.

With the same fixed rule on evaluation text beyond the control prefix used in P-L1-007, bilateral JS gives 24 genuine wins and 6 decoy wins across 30 repeats (six language/contrast strata, five seeds each). Its frozen cutoff accepts 14/30 genuine candidates and 0/30 decoys. Left-only JS and the inherited eight-rule prose loss each tie all 30 times and accept 5/30 candidates of each origin at their separately calibrated cutoffs.

Evaluation wins by contrast: English in/is 4/5, an/at 5/5; Latin re/ra 5/5, us/um 0/5; Italian la/le 5/5 and ra/ri 5/5. Seeds reuse the same text and are not independent language samples. The us/um reversal is stable under all five fixed seeds.

At half matched-pool replacement with exact-left matching, bilateral JS gives 26 genuine wins and 4 decoy wins; the cutoff accepts 11/30 genuine candidates and 1/30 decoys. These are secondary sensitivity results with the full-coverage calibration cutoff retained.

Matching only word-boundary positions, without equal incoming contexts, reduces full-coverage evaluation performance to 16 genuine and 14 decoy wins. The frozen bilateral cutoff accepts 8/30 genuine candidates and 0/30 decoys. This limits transfer beyond the primary matched-left design.

Matching both incoming and outgoing glyph counts forces equal left and right probability distributions for X and Z, so both JS scores tie. All 30 full-coverage evaluation trials and all 25 supported half-coverage evaluation trials behave this way. Five half-coverage trials fail the preregistered minimum support; exclusions are retained in the tables.

Under the same frozen cutoff, bilateral JS accepts no candidates among 118 scored letter/component combinations on three untouched natural streams and no candidates among 2368 combinations on sixty new first-order direct-emission streams. All sixty chains emit one glyph at a time without a fusion operation. The corresponding left-only JS cutoff accepts 45 generated-text combinations across 31 of the 60 streams; inherited eight-rule raw-loss cutoff accepts none. These finite and dependent controls do not prove a zero general false-positive rate.

A separate entropy-form implementation verifies 1440 paired JS values and 4972 negative-control JS values, with maximum absolute discrepancy 9.43689570931383e-16 and identical cutoff decisions. Independent cumulative-table sampling regenerates all sixty chain hashes; hashes of the three natural streams also match.
limitations: The evaluated objects are planted substitutions in normalized public natural text, not manuscript signs. No manuscript result or decipherment claim is made.

Six selected contrasts in three languages are the evidence units; five seeds per contrast are robustness repetitions. Training, calibration and evaluation use different blocks/windows from the same pinned books, not independent authors or genres.

The empirical negative cutoff pools thirty related calibration trials. Zero observed decoy/negative acceptances in evaluation does not bound the population false-positive rate without additional assumptions.

The new statistic uses normalized raw adjacency distributions including spaces, while the inherited score uses trimmed incidence entries. The baseline here is a separately calibrated raw loss, not the paper's original five-percent rank criterion.

Partial planting and grammar can change the residual component contexts. The stable us/um reversal and weaker word-position-only result show that adding right context does not eliminate this confounding.
All matching, support, seed, cutoff and sample-window rules were frozen publicly before their corresponding evaluation. No outcome-driven retuning was performed.
